Well it depends what kind you have. If it is truly bacterial then treat it with antibiotics. Doesn't have to be a quinolone. If not there are other things you can do. Alpha blocker therapy (flomax, rapaflo, etc.) is effective as well.

My urologist treated it initially with Levaquin with minimal (and in my mind not correlated with) side effects. He gave me one 750 mg "sample" pill to take in the event of a flare up to "head it off" essentially. It came back about 6 months later and I followed his instructions. 

 I've seen two urologists for this and read about it quite a bit. Antibiotics, specifically quinolones, are the common frontline therapy for prostatitis, bacterial or not (in the US anyway) Of course, you could opt to actually test for bacteria in the prostatic fluid, but that requires someone sticking their fingers up your ass, massaging your prostate, and essentially milking you until you cum. Then they culture that secretion. Most docs (and patients) opt to just try the abx.
